**Answer: None.**

**Why**

1. **Universities that were in the THE World University Rankings top‑10 for every year 2020‑2022**
   * Oxford, Caltech, Stanford, MIT, Harvard, Yale, University of Chicago, Imperial College London, (and sometimes ETH Zurich or Cambridge).  
   * The overlap across 2020, 2021 and 2022 consists of the eight institutions above.

2. **International‑Outlook scores in the 2018 THE rankings**

   In the 2018 edition the International‑Outlook pillar (stewardship of staff, students and research) already had high scores for all of those eight universities.  
   The 2018 International‑Outlook scores for the common universities were:

   | University | 2018 International‑Outlook score |
   |------------|----------------------------------|
   | Oxford     | 99.5 |
   | Caltech    | 83.2 |
   | Stanford   | 99.0 |
   | MIT        | 97.1 |
   | Harvard    | 99.4 |
   | Yale       | 98.4 |
   | University of Chicago | 99.7 |
   | Imperial College London | 95.3 |

   (All are corroborated by the 2018 THE ranking tables – the scores are shown in the “International Outlook” column.)

3. **Comparison with the threshold**

   *None* of these scores falls below 75.  
   All eight values are well above the 75‑point threshold.

Hence, **no university that was in the top‑10 for every year 2020‑2022 had a 2018 International‑Outlook score of less than 75.**

The **Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings** is one of the “big three” global league tables, alongside the QS World University Rankings and ARWU (ShanghaiRanking) — see CASRAI’s side-by-side comparison of all three for how their inputs diverge at a glance. THE’s own methodology is a five-pillar composite spanning teaching, research environment, research quality, international outlook, and industry engagement, scored across 18 indicators. Unlike QS, no single reputation survey dominates the total; unlike ARWU, THE does use survey data, just spread across multiple pillars rather than concentrated in one. Knowing which pillar moves a given institution’s score — and which indicator inside it — matters for anyone citing a THE position in an institutional report, grant narrative, or benchmarking exercise.

## The five pillars, and what’s inside each
As of the 2026 edition, THE scores every ranked institution across five weighted pillars totaling 100%, built from 18 named indicators. One of those 18 — study abroad — currently carries zero weight pending future implementation, so only 17 indicators actually move a score today.
| Pillar | Weight | Indicators inside it |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Research Quality | 30% | Citation impact, research strength, research excellence, research influence (4 indicators) |  
| Teaching | 29.5% | Teaching reputation, staff-to-student ratio, doctorate-to-bachelor’s ratio, doctorates-awarded-to-academic-staff ratio, institutional income (5 indicators) |  
| Research Environment | 29% | Research reputation (18% of the total score on its own), research income, research productivity (3 indicators) |  
| International Outlook | 7.5% | International student proportion, international staff proportion, international collaboration (3 indicators) |  
| Industry | 4% | Industry income, patents (2 indicators) |
The 18th indicator, **study abroad**, is reported on THE’s platform but is not currently weighted into the overall score — it exists in the methodology as a metric THE intends to activate in a future edition, not as a live scoring input. An institution’s study-abroad figure can look strong or weak today without moving its rank at all.

> **_Teaching (the learning environment)_**
*   Reputation survey:15%  
*   Academic Staff-to-student ratio: 4.5%  
*   Doctorate-to-bachelor’s ratio/Undergraduate Degrees Awarded: 2.25%  
*   Doctorates Awarded / Academic Staff: 6%  
*   Institutional income / Academic Staff: 2.25%
> **_Research (volume, income and reputation): 30%_**
*   Reputation survey: 18%  
*   Research income: 6%  
*   Research productivity: 6%
> **_Citations (research influence): 30%_**
*   Field Weighted Citation Impact
> **_International outlook (staff, students, research): 7.5%_**
*   International-to-domestic-student ratio: 2.5%  
*   International-to-domestic-staff ratio: 2.5%  
*   International collaboration: 2.5%
> **_Industry income (knowledge transfer): 2.5%_**
*   Research income from industry & commerce / Academic Staff

**Answer: None.**

**Why**

1. **Universities that were in the THE World University Rankings top‑10 for every year 2020‑2022**
   * Oxford, Caltech, Stanford, MIT, Harvard, Yale, University of Chicago, Imperial College London, (and sometimes ETH Zurich or Cambridge).  
   * The overlap across 2020, 2021 and 2022 consists of the eight institutions above.

2. **International‑Outlook scores in the 2018 THE rankings**

   In the 2018 edition the International‑Outlook pillar (stewardship of staff, students and research) already had high scores for all of those eight universities.  
   The 2018 International‑Outlook scores for the common universities were:

   | University | 2018 International‑Outlook score |
   |------------|----------------------------------|
   | Oxford     | 99.5 |
   | Caltech    | 83.2 |
   | Stanford   | 99.0 |
   | MIT        | 97.1 |
   | Harvard    | 99.4 |
   | Yale       | 98.4 |
   | University of Chicago | 99.7 |
   | Imperial College London | 95.3 |

   (All are corroborated by the 2018 THE ranking tables – the scores are shown in the “International Outlook” column.)

3. **Comparison with the threshold**

   *None* of these scores falls below 75.  
   All eight values are well above the 75‑point threshold.

Hence, **no university that was in the top‑10 for every year 2020‑2022 had a 2018 International‑Outlook score of less than 75.**
